design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (creditor_client_services, category client).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {prerequisite_problems: 1, problems: 2, factor_counts: [5, 5]}. Tree = root + 1 prerequisite; client_ext_early_termination_charge takes 5 factors, client_ext_closing_settlement_payment takes 5. Edge must be value_input (max(1-1,1)=1).
[Scope snapshot] Occupied before: nothing (first task). Claimed: client_ext_early_termination_charge (agent, tool book_early_termination_charge_4cc8362c, event client_early_termination_fee_assessed) and client_ext_closing_settlement_payment (user, tool pay_closing_fee_settlement_180c3708, event client_fee_payment_received for an agreement under termination notice). Left for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [6,5]): late charges on a past-due invoice (client_late_charge_assessed) and the client's payment of a named past-due invoice (a different payment object, scoped to one invoice, not to the closing of an agreement), plus remittance, recall, credit and terms policies untouched. The DSL can only aggregate this agreement's client tables and the client's own legal/flatfee holdings (account-level data such as balance_due or stage is unreadable for a creditor-client customer), which is why the claimed quantities are agreement-level single-instance figures: one termination charge per notice, one closing settlement per agreement.
[Design thesis] Surface goal: 'we gave termination notice; let me pay everything we owe on the agreement today'. Core scored values: the closing settlement payment (423.74) and, hidden behind it, the early-termination charge (206.66) that the closing rule waits on. Chain: surface goal -> closing settlement rule's prerequisite sentence ('The closing settlement payment is worked out only after the agreement's fees owed carry the early-termination charge due for the termination notice on record.') -> ledger shows no such charge though a notice inside the initial term is on record -> early-termination rule (5 factors) -> booking -> closing settlement (5 factors) -> customer's own payment. Depth 2 problems; breadth: notice request, agreement dates/tier, 37 ledger rows (invoices, payments, credits, late charge, collections, reversals, remittances), legal agreement + matter ledger, flatfee program + unit ledger.
[Why a good test] The agent must (a) discover from the closing rule that a termination charge has to stand first, (b) find in the termination rule that a notice inside the initial term makes it due on the notice date, (c) compute it with a day-count proration and three reductions scaled by a goodwill share drawn from two other products' records, (d) then compute a settlement that nets trust only against open invoices after two reserves, a prompt discount on the charge just booked and a late-charge waiver, and (e) hand the payment to the client. Missing (a) gives 237.75; reading only the computation documents gives 1500.00 and 797.45.
[Problem-tree card] root client_ext_closing_settlement_payment (user) <- client_ext_early_termination_charge (agent). Edge: kind value_input, gate termination_charge (compute binding of the root), form state, policy_source = the sentence above (affirmative direction: a charge-style figure 'is worked out only after' what it rests on), condition: an early-termination charge entry dated the notice's request date stands on the agreement and fees owed include it; resolved_by book_early_termination_charge_4cc8362c. Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (an entry kind standing on the agreement's money history + the fees owed balance) and names no action or tool; no code tokens; scope = exactly the one charge due for the notice on record. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a client_early_termination_fee_assessed entry: the early-termination rule ('...booked on the date the notice was received') whose target tool is the only tool writing that event. Derivation: sentence -> records (notice 2026-10-06 naming 2026-12-31 < term end 2027-02-28, no termination-charge entry) -> early-termination rule -> book the charge. False at opening: initial_state.client_service_requests.<notice>.request_date=2026-10-06, requested_effective_date=2026-12-31, client_agreements.term_end_date=2027-02-28, fees_receivable=590.79 with no termination-charge row. Flips: booking 206.66 -> termination_charge 0->206.66, fees 590.79->797.45. Deletion sensitivity (run): root recomputes 237.75 instead of 423.74. Topological order: charge (step 10) then payment (step 12). user_scenario never mentions a charge, fee or prior booking; tools validate nothing.
[Base-invariant card] ETF write subject client_early_termination_fee_assessed is governed only by client_evt_termination_and_renewal; its gates runoff_period_over (applies to client_agreement_closed) and client_notice_on_record (applies to client_runoff_started) do not apply to this event, so base_preconditions carries policy_scope with the notice row and the term end as evidence; the clause 'A termination that takes effect before the end of the initial term carries the early_termination_fee_usd, charged on the date the notice was received' is superseded in overwrite by the extended sentence (amount figured by this rule, still booked on the notice date). Payment subject client_fee_payment_received is governed only by client_evt_fee_billing (its only gate late_charge_start_reached applies to late charges) -> policy_scope; the base offset clause is superseded for the closing settlement only. No time gate applies to either write, so temporal_feasibility is []. Date conventions used: DAYS(notice, named)=86 (end-exclusive difference), unexpired = DAYS(notice, term end) - 86 = 59, initial term = DAYS(2026-03-01, 2027-02-28) = 364.
[Business-object card] Object of the charge: the agreement's single termination notice (service request, received, request_date 2026-10-06). Object of the payment: the whole fees owed on that agreement (no invoice named). Rows entering: client_fee_invoiced x7 (2372.25), client_fee_payment_received x5 (1448.50), client_fee_credit_issued x2 (336.00, reversed-collection credits on CI-526081 and CI-526091 for the 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-29 returns), late charge x1 (3.04 on CI-526041), collections x13 of which the 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-06 collections (1660.00) are the unremitted trust, reversals x2, remittances x7 (6525.00). Excluded: remittance rows from open invoices; the authorized-but-unfiled 2026-09-28 legal matter from the suit count; the flatfee paid-in-full status report from the conversion count.
[Factor card — client_ext_early_termination_charge, 5 factors (1 method, 4 parameter)] baseline (computation document): full 1500.00 fee when effect precedes the initial-term end, booked on the notice date. (1) unexpired_term_proration, method, evidence agreement dates + tier term: tiers 'no more than half unexpired and term >= 24 months -> pro rata by whole 30-day months', 'no more than half unexpired and term < 24 months -> pro rata by calendar days', 'otherwise full fee'; taken: days tier (59/364, 12-month Preferred term) -> 243.1319; baseline-substitution result 1275.00. (2) legal_forwarding_reduction, parameter, cross-difficulty legal, multi-source (legal status AND suits filed in 12 months): 40%/20%/0; taken 20% (suits 2026-06-30, 2026-08-27); near-miss: 2026-09-28 matter only authorized; substitution 230.98. (3) notice_lead_reduction, parameter, evidence notice and named dates: >=1.5x notice -> 10%, >=1.25x and <1.5x -> 5%, else 0; taken 5% (86 days vs 60; 90 would have been needed for 10%); substitution 212.74. (4) precollect_conversion_reduction, parameter, cross-difficulty flatfee, multi-source (program status AND conversions in 12 months): 10%/5%/0; taken 5% (conversions 2026-07-22, 2026-09-14); near-miss: the 2026-06-09 paid_in_full debtor report is not a conversion; substitution 212.74. (5) late_charge_goodwill, parameter, evidence client ledger: >=3 late charges -> keep 0, 1-2 -> keep half, none -> keep all; taken half (one late charge 2026-07-15); substitution 170.19. Whole baseline 1500.00. Rationale of the ladders: an exit late in the term is prorated as the business does for unexpired commitments; continuing legal suits and pre-collect conversions keep revenue flowing to Ridgeline after the exit; generous notice eases runoff staffing; recent late payment forfeits part of the goodwill reductions.
[Factor card — client_ext_closing_settlement_payment, 5 factors (1 method, 4 parameter)] baseline: fees owed on the day of payment (797.45 at handling time). (1) trust_offset_method, method, evidence remittance basis + tier offset permission + invoice/payment/credit ledger: net_remit -> trust against all fees; gross_remit with offset allowed -> trust against open invoiced fees only; otherwise nothing; taken gross+offset (Preferred fees_offset_against_remittance true) -> min(350.00, 587.75)=350.00; substitution 773.74. (2) returned_payment_reserve, parameter: >=3 returns in 6 months -> reserve all of last month's collections, 1-2 -> half, none -> 0; taken half (2 returns) -> 830.00 of 1660.00; substitution 185.99 (the cap at open invoices then binds). (3) legal_cost_reserve, parameter, cross-difficulty legal, multi-source (status AND cost advance): active & advance>0 -> whole advance, suspended & advance>0 -> half, else 0; taken active -> 480.00; substitution 185.99. (4) prompt_settlement_discount, parameter, evidence notice date vs handling date: <=10 days -> 10% of the termination charge, 11-30 -> 5%, else 0; taken 10% (8 days) -> 20.666; substitution 444.41. (5) closing_late_charge_waiver, parameter: exactly one late charge in 12 months -> waive in full, exactly two -> half, else none; taken full -> 3.04; substitution 426.78. Whole baseline 797.45.
[Rule <-> compute sweep] Forward: every world-reading or branching binding of both policies carries a verbatim rule quotation in compute_basis (notice/named dates, unexpired days, proration ladder, each reduction ladder, goodwill ladder, combination 'first added into one reduction share ... reduced once', rounding at the end; open invoiced fees definition, both reserves, the netting ladder, discount and waiver ladders, final 'all taken off the same fees owed, never less than zero and rounded to the cent once at the end'). Reverse: the rule's promises — later-of effective date, initial-term end = term end while not renewed, nothing owed at/after the end (result guard 'if unexpired_days > 0 else 0'), whole months = complete 30-day spans counted down (int()), reductions combined not successive, trust never below zero (MX) and never above open invoices (MN) — each map to a binding. No binding carries a filter the rule does not state.
[Seed] SEED-FRESH world: 1 creditor-client customer, 1 Preferred agreement (balances equal ledger sums: trust 9235.00-1050.00-6525.00=1660.00; fees 2372.25+3.04-1448.50-336.00=590.79), 37 client ledger rows, 1 termination notice request, legal agreement (Agency-Advanced, active, advance 480.00 = 960.00 disbursed - 480.00 reimbursed (one client reimbursement per cost: 395.00 filing fee and 85.00 service on matter KLG-5260522-04)) with 11 matter rows, flatfee 300-unit program (310 units bought, 6 used, 1 credited = 305) with 11 rows. Consumer-side rows are not seeded because no client-service read can reach them; client ledger account references are therefore left empty and source_txn_id keeps the consumer payment reference. Automatic-clause check: every closed period was remitted within SLA and invoiced within 5 business days; both returned payments already carry their reversed-collection credits; CI-526081 (due 2026-10-08) reaches its late-charge start only on 2026-10-18 and CI-526091 is not due, so no late charge is owed at 2026-10-14; the fees-past-due hold limit (invoice + 30 + 60 days) is far off; the termination takes effect 2026-12-31 so runoff has not started; tier review is 2027-03-01. Nothing outside the tree is owed.
[Persona] Wendeline Abernathy-Kopp, controller, brisk; volunteers the notice date and the wish to pay off everything today herself; gives phone 6165555472 and EIN last four 5318 only when asked; agrees in one line if told something must be put on the agreement first; pays exactly the amount handed to her via the user tool; reads back the confirmation and ends. She never names a termination charge, never quotes a figure, never asks for anything beyond the settlement.
[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, EIN last4) -> find_client_agreements -> find_client_service_requests -> find_client_ledger -> find_legal_agreements -> find_legal_matter_events -> find_flatfee_programs -> find_flatfee_unit_ledger -> unlock+call book_early_termination_charge_4cc8362c(agreement, 2026-10-06, 206.66) -> unlock_user + call_user pay_closing_fee_settlement_180c3708(agreement, 423.74).
[Verification run] /tmp authoring harness replayed the gold with the real tools and evaluated compute on handling-time snapshots: ETF 206.66 (branches 16), sensitivities {proration 1275.00, legal 230.98, lead 212.74, precollect 212.74, goodwill 170.19}, baseline 1500.00; closing payment 423.74 (branches 17), sensitivities {trust 773.74, reserve 185.99, legal 185.99, prompt 444.41, waiver 426.78}, baseline 797.45; with the charge booking skipped the payment recomputes 237.75. Gates run: check_extended / check_task_tools / replay_tasks / check_solvability / check_compute / check_grounding / check_cross_fire --task 0 all OK.
[Revisions] (1) replay FK: empty-string ids counted as dangling -> set unused id fields to null. (2) replay closure: consumer accounts, account entries and consumer profiles were seeded but no client-service read touches them -> dropped them and cleared client-ledger/legal account references; seed_consistency evidence re-pointed to client ledger fields; re-ran all gates green. (3) overwrite replaced_by of the closing policy initially did not match the rule (case and trailing punctuation) -> quoted exactly.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] Using only the published rules, tool schemas, the finder returns and the persona: the client asks to settle everything; the closing rule says the figure is worked out only after the termination charge stands; the ledger has none while a 2026-10-06 notice naming 2026-12-31 is on record; the termination rule gives 206.66 as above; the closing rule then gives 423.74. Same object, order and values as gold; no second reading found (notice-lead tiers are disjoint by their 'less than' clause; whole-month tier does not apply to a 12-month term).
[Rework r2 — policy-task audit audits/policy_task/creditor_client_services r1]
0-F1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED) symptom: two cross-category seed rows broke their own product charters. Root cause: the flatfee and legal histories were laid down without the flatfee series/conversion rule and the legal one-cost reimbursement grain and costs_first recovery order. Change: (a) the CHH-5120561 conversion moved from 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-14 — the debtor was submitted 2026-06-23, the 300-unit series is 5 letters with the last at +75 days (by 2026-09-08), conversion_requires_series_complete is true and the 45-day conversion window is respected; the other conversion (CHH-5120031, submitted 2026-04-14, series ended by 2026-06-30, converted 2026-07-22) already complied. Conversions in 12 months stay 2 -> 5 percent. (b) the single 547.50 reimbursement was replaced by two one-cost client reimbursements on matter KLG-5260522-04 (filing fee 395.00, service 85.00, 2026-09-15), so that matter's unreimbursed costs are 0.00; the second matter was re-dated (authorized 2026-07-10, filed 2026-08-27 within the 60-day validity, costs 2026-08-27 and 2026-09-03, matter KLG-5260710-05) so the 2026-08-19 collection on it precedes its costs and the costs_first recovery order is not engaged; its 480.00 of costs are within the 750.00 per-matter advance cap. cost_advance_balance is now 960.00 - 480.00 = 480.00. Suits filed in 12 months stay 2 (2026-06-30, 2026-08-27) -> 20 percent. Re-run: ETC 206.66 unchanged (sensitivities 1275.00/230.98/212.74/212.74/170.19); closing payment 356.24 -> 423.74 (legal reserve 480.00, available trust 1660.00 - 830.00 - 480.00 = 350.00, met 350.00; sensitivities trust 773.74, reserve 185.99, legal 185.99, prompt 444.41, waiver 426.78; baseline 797.45; skipped prerequisite 237.75). Propagated to the gold argument, computations, tracing, prerequisite_closure, seed_consistency and this dossier.
0-O1 change: the seeded 2026-07-15 late charge on CI-526041 re-figured under the extended late-charge rule at its own date: 3.04 (rate 1.25 = 1.50 - 0.25 for a pack paid in 19 of 30 days but 3 months old; 70 days old, no step; no other late-charged invoice -> percentage alone 3.38125; legal active with deposit at its 0.00 minimum -> 10 percent relief) instead of the base-formula 5.00; fees_receivable 592.75 -> 590.79. The waiver moves with it, so the payment is unaffected by this row (fees owed 797.45 after the charge).
0-O2 change: the readings the audit weighed are now pinned in the rules themselves: the ETC rule says 'Each such count is the difference between the two dates in calendar days: the first date is not counted and the last date is counted.' (59/364), and all four rules say 'A window of a number of months before a date covers the dates after the same day that number of months earlier, up to and including that date.' (the reserve's 'month before the payment' is 2026-09-15..2026-10-14, 1660.00).
0-O3 response: in the gross-with-offset tier the open-invoice cap (587.75) does not bind (350.00 is met), so on this world it coincides with the net tier; making the cap bind would make both reserves decorative (available trust above open invoices), which the factor gate forbids. The method still bears weight against its fall-through (773.74). Recorded, no change.
Charter-level items also closed in r2: D1 precedence sentences (closing rule: 'Where a termination notice is on record, a payment of the fees owed on that agreement is a closing settlement payment even when the client names one of its invoices.'; payoff scoped to 'an agreement with no termination notice on record'); D2 suit and conversion counts scoped to the legal agreement / program naming this agreement (legal_agreement_ref, precollect_program_ref); D3 renewal test added ('The agreement has renewed when its term end date lies the tier's initial_term_months or more whole months after its effective date ...', binding renewed = MONTHS(effective, term end) >= initial_term_months, 11 < 12 here); D4 net_remit deviation declared in the closing policy's overwrite against client_evt_remittance. Re-ran all per-task gates green.
user_scenario: You are Wendeline Abernathy-Kopp, controller of Coldwater Hearth & Home Furnishings, Inc., a furniture retailer in Kentwood, Michigan that places its unpaid retail installment accounts with Ridgeline Recovery Associates. You are brisk, organised and a little pressed for time, speaking in short, practical sentences. Coldwater is bringing collections in-house, and on October 6 your team submitted a termination notice for your contingency agreement through Ridgeline's client portal, naming December 31 as the date you wanted it to end. You are calling today because you want to settle everything Coldwater owes Ridgeline on that agreement with one payment, today, so your finance team can close the account on their side; you are authorised to make the payment yourself, and you want to make it yourself rather than wait for an invoice. You open by saying roughly that: who you are, that you sent the termination notice on October 6, and that you want to pay off whatever you owe on the agreement today. You have no idea of the exact figure; you think the open fee invoices come to a few hundred dollars, but you expect the representative to tell you the number. You give your details only when asked: the company's collections line on file is 6165555472, and the last four digits of Coldwater's EIN are 5318; if asked for the company name you say Coldwater Hearth & Home Furnishings, Inc. If asked, you confirm the notice was sent on October 6 and named December 31, and that Coldwater has only the one contingency agreement with Ridgeline. If the representative asks about your legal forwarding programme or your pre-collect letter program, you say nothing about them is changing on this call. If asked whether you want to pay a particular invoice, you say no, you want everything owed on the agreement settled as part of the termination. If the representative explains that something has to be put on the agreement before the settlement figure can be worked out, you say that is fine and they should go ahead, because you would rather have everything wrapped up in one settlement; you do not ask for details beyond a one-line explanation. Once the representative tells you the settlement amount and hands the payment over to you, you make the payment on the agreement yourself for exactly the amount they gave you. You do not argue with the figure, you do not suggest a different number, and you never correct the representative's method. When you receive the payment confirmation, you read the confirmation reference back once, thank the representative and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the creditor client's profile from the main collections telephone number the caller gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the client's customer reference; nothing may be disclosed before the profile is found and verified.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller against two details on file: the collections telephone number and the last four digits of the EIN.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Ridgeline transacts no client business before identity verification passes (2 matching details).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the contingency agreement: tier (Preferred), status active, effective date 2026-03-01, term end 2027-02-28, gross_remit monthly, trust held 1660.00 and fees owed 590.79.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier fixes the early-termination fee (1500.00), the termination notice days (60), the initial term (12 months) and the fee-offset permission; the dates fix the unexpired term; the balances are the base of the closing settlement.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the termination notice on record: received 2026-10-06 naming 2026-12-31 as the effective date.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The notice date anchors the effective date, the notice-lead reduction and the prompt-settlement discount; its presence is what makes an early-termination charge due, and the charge is not yet on the ledger — the state the closing settlement's prerequisite sentence waits on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole client money history: invoices, fee payments, fee credits, the 2026-07-15 late charge, collections (including the October collections still held in trust), the two returned-payment reversals and the remittances; no early-termination charge entry exists.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows the closing settlement cannot be fixed yet (no early-termination charge carried, per 'The closing settlement payment is worked out only after the agreement's fees owed carry the early-termination charge due for the termination notice on record.'); supplies the late-charge count for the goodwill share and the late-charge waiver, the open invoiced fees, the returned-payment count and last month's collections for the trust reserve.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's legal forwarding agreement naming this contingency agreement: Agency-Advanced Cost Suit Program, active, unreimbursed cost advance 480.00.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Its status decides the legal forwarding reduction of the early-termination charge, and its status and cost advance decide the legal cost reserve of the closing settlement.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Count the suits filed under the legal agreement in the 12 months before 2026-10-14 (2026-06-30 and 2026-08-27; the 2026-09-28 matter is only authorized).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The number of suits filed selects the 20 percent tier of the legal forwarding reduction.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's flat-fee pre-collect program naming this agreement for conversions: First Notice 300-Unit Program, active.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The program's status is one condition of the pre-collect reduction of the early-termination charge.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Count the debtors converted to contingency collection in the trailing 12 months (2026-07-22 and 2026-09-14; the 2026-06-09 paid-in-full report is not a conversion).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The conversion count selects the 5 percent tier of the pre-collect reduction.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the early-termination charge booking tool.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect; unlocked once.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Book the early-termination charge of 206.66 dated 2026-10-06, raising fees owed from 590.79 to 797.45.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: client_ext_early_termination_charge computes charge_amount; the closing settlement waits on this charge standing on the agreement (value_input).

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: Value: the agreement reference returned by find_client_agreements for this client (the only agreement it holds). Basis: the tool docstring 'the placement agreement reference number (agreement id) of the creditor client's contingency agreement being charged, read from the placement agreement lookup'; the termination notice on record (find_client_service_requests) names the same agreement. Uniqueness: the client holds one agreement, and the charge belongs to the agreement the notice was given on.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.notice_date: Value: 2026-10-06. Basis: the rule 'The charge is booked on the date the notice was received, rounded to the cent.' and the notice request's request_date 2026-10-06 returned by find_client_service_requests. Uniqueness: one termination notice is on record; its received date is the only date the rule allows, not today's date (2026-10-14) and not the named effective date (2026-12-31).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_amount: Value: 206.66. Factors: (1) unexpired_term_proration — effective date is the later of 2026-10-06 + 60 days and the named 2026-12-31, i.e. 86 days after notice; unexpired initial term = 145 - 86 = 59 days of a 364-day initial term (2026-03-01..2027-02-28), no more than half, and the Preferred initial term is 12 months (<24) so the 1500.00 fee is prorated by days: 1500 x 59/364 = 243.1319 (baseline: full 1500.00); (2) legal_forwarding_reduction — the Agency-Advanced legal agreement is active and 2 suits were filed in the trailing 12 months (2026-06-30, 2026-08-27; the 2026-09-28 matter is only authorized) -> 20 percent; (3) notice_lead_reduction — 86 days given vs 60 required: at least 1.25x (75) but under 1.5x (90) -> 5 percent; (4) precollect_conversion_reduction — the First Notice 300-Unit program is active with 2 conversions in 12 months -> 5 percent; (5) late_charge_goodwill — one late charge (2026-07-15) in 12 months -> half the reduction share kept. Reduction share = (0.20+0.05+0.05) x 0.5 = 0.15, applied once: 243.1319 x 0.85 = 206.662 -> 206.66.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the client's closing settlement payment tool so the caller can make the payment herself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the customer's own write; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The client pays its closing fee settlement of 423.74 on the agreement.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: client_ext_closing_settlement_payment computes payment_amount on the world after the early-termination charge is booked; it is the root problem the caller asked for.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: Value: the same agreement reference returned by find_client_agreements and used for the termination charge. Basis: the tool docstring 'the placement agreement reference number (agreement id) of the agreement being settled, which the representative reads from the placement agreement lookup and gives to the client'. Uniqueness: the client holds one agreement and asked to settle what it owes on it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_amount: Value: 423.74. Factors on the world after the termination charge is booked: fees owed 797.45 (open invoices 587.75 + late charge 3.04 + termination charge 206.66); (1) trust_offset_method — gross_remit with fees_offset_against_remittance true on Preferred -> available trust is set against the open invoiced fees 587.75 only; (2) returned_payment_reserve — 2 returned-payment reversals in 6 months (2026-08-18, 2026-09-29) -> half of the 1660.00 collected in the last month = 830.00 reserved; (3) legal_cost_reserve — legal agreement active with a 480.00 cost advance -> 480.00 reserved; available trust = 1660.00 - 830.00 - 480.00 = 350.00, met from trust = min(350.00, 587.75) = 350.00; (4) prompt_settlement_discount — paid 8 days after the 2026-10-06 notice -> 10 percent of 206.66 = 20.666; (5) closing_late_charge_waiver — exactly one late charge in 12 months -> its 3.04 waived. Payment = 797.45 - 350.00 - 20.666 - 3.04 = 423.744 -> 423.74 (baseline, fees owed alone: 797.45).

factor_trace: unexpired_term_proration (method): notice 2026-10-06, named date 2026-12-31 -> 86 days to effect (> the 60-day notice), unexpired initial term 59 of 364 days (no more than half) and a 12-month initial term -> pro rata by days: 1500.00 x 59/364 = 243.1319; baseline (full fee) 1500.00 -> result 1275.00.
